restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes; each is one padded block M || 0x86 with zero capacity (520 fixed state bits). Complete fixed-zero-IV SHA3-256 sponge with suffix 0x06 and pad10*1, prefix rounds 0..4, 256-bit digest.

No advice: the algorithm runs every phase itself - the trail search P, the advice program B', setup S, the connector and the enumeration E - and the claimed time is the sum of caps and exact counts times counted prices (proof 2, 6): P (deterministic) at its exact counts times the longest counted paths (T1 8,674,833 nodes x 2^12; T2 1,639,088,128 leaves x 166; T3 5,679,328,446 bitsliced batches x 1,583, every batch charged in full; full evaluations at F_CAP = 2^22 x 2^13; 1411 group setups x 2^27; batches, groups and leaves recomputed by r5-trail-0..3, prices by r5-count): 2^32.71 units; B' at 2^32 units plus at most one counter update, at most 2^26 units per candidate (CCAP); at most 2^13 connector attempts of at most 2^18 work units; E: K = 96 spaces of 2^24 batches of 256 pairs (one per bit of a 256-bit word) at 6,112 primitives per batch on every path (2^32.76); at most 2^11 stage-2 pairs per space. Total 2^34.1359, claimed 34.14. No expected value is charged.

E is v8's E as a function of the space (proof Lemma 4): the same 2^32 pairs and the same 24 round-2 equations, evaluated bitsliced; r5-count checks every equation word against a plain evaluation. P outputs v8's trail (two native runs of the batch form of T3, proof 2.1 and Appendix A). The only count of P the organizer cannot recompute is the number F of full evaluations (pass 2: 770; pass 1, an upper bound: 1,896,302); it enters only through F_CAP = 2^22. That P outputs the trail of proof 3 within F_CAP is a stated deterministic premise from those runs (1.4 x 10^12 leaves; commands, sources and log hashes in Appendix A).

Development runs are not charged and are disclosed (proof 0, unchanged from v8): they fixed the six B' design constants R = 16, DMIN = 40 and the weights KW = 1.0, MW = 0.25, LB = 1.0, PREF = 1.0 (75 processes, 1,559 CPU-s); uncharged v5 runs set the connector's DMIN = 33 and its 2^18 work-unit cap (charged in full, never bound). Every success rate used comes from runs made after the constants were fixed: the v6 full-scale run and pre-registrations A and B. Sensitivity, not claimed: charging B''s development at 2^38 primitives per core-second gives 38.29, v7's whole development ledger 41.22. The constants new in v9 and v10 (batch layouts, CCAP, K = 96, A_ADV = 2^11, A_MAX = 2^13, B_BUDGET = 2^32) only change cost or caps and were set by counting and by the bound of proof 5, with no new run.

Probability space: fresh algorithmic coins, fixed target, no advice. Success >= 1 - 0.0320 - 0.0065 - 2^-41 - (1 - 0.013)^96 - 2^-13 > 0.67 under H1 (for each advice B' can output, per accepted space E outputs a pair with probability >= 0.013), H2 (B' candidates within CCAP) and H3 (connector acceptance of B' outputs); claimed 0.40, which needs s >= 0.0060 for the final advice (2.2 times below s0) and, at s = s0, q >= 0.0258 per B' candidate (2.9 times below q_c0).

Executed evidence (not the claimed cost, unchanged from v8): the pre-registered v6 full-scale run (14 collisions in 512 spaces; denominator and numerator re-executed by r5-den-0..2 and r5-replay); pre-registration A: nine B' runs (all outputs, 2^23.4-2^28.2 units; every candidate at most 2^25.848 units, below CCAP) each followed by 128 connector attempts (45-120 accepted); pre-registration B: E on 2 spaces per advice (round-2 passes 1.033 x the trail value; 3 collisions with fresh advice, replayed by r5-replay8). r5-bp-0..4 re-derive every B' output and run 288 organizer-seeded connector attempts; r5-bpfull executes B' whole with its budget and candidate-cap counters.

Th0rgal is a co-author: 7deb1595 (with Subflatus3 and rubenmarcus) gave the zero-advice framing used here (v8's E also used its early-abort row order; v10's bitsliced E evaluates all equations). Memory: largest phase about 224 MB (T3's triple tables in the counted program); declared 30.

The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement over published work; no improvement on the method of Guo et al. is claimed beyond the byte-aligned adaptation, B', the bitsliced counted E and T3 and the accounting.

heuristics.statement: For each advice (beta1', beta0') that B' can output and one connector attempt with fresh coins that is accepted on it, the enumeration E (proof 2.4) on its 2^32-pair window outputs a pair (all 24 round-2 equations hold and the 256-bit digests are equal) with probability at least s0 = 0.013, and the stage-2 cap of 2^11 pairs per space does not bind. This is a bound per advice, not an average over advices.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability: given the final advice, the K = 96 accepted spaces are i.i.d. (independent coins), so Pr[no output] = (1 - s)^96 <= 0.2848; the claimed 0.40 needs s >= 0.0060 for the final advice. Output correctness and every cost cap hold without H1.
heuristics.extrapolation: Pre-registered v6 full-scale run with the advice that the shipped B' reproduces from LABEL_B within its budget (k = 0; r5-bp-0): E output a pair in 14 of the first 512 accepted spaces (s-hat = 0.0273; one-sided 99% Clopper-Pearson lower bound 0.0133 >= s0); r5-den-0..2 re-run all 538 attempt indices up to the 512th accepted one (the whole denominator) and r5-replay re-derives the 14 positives. Across advice (Markov premise: E depends on the advice only through the exact 2-round difference alpha2, which every advice reaches): pre-registration B enumerated 2 spaces of each of the 9 advices of pre-registration A: 4,760 round-2 passes against 4,608 expected (ratio 1.033, per advice 0.975-1.125), and 3 collisions in 16 spaces of fresh advice (k = 4 and 7), replayed by r5-replay8. Largest stage-2 count per space: 307 (E check) and 301 (v6), against the cap 2,048. E premise: v10's E tests the same pairs with the same predicate as the E of these runs (proof Lemma 4, r5-count). Sampling premise: SHAKE-256-expanded coins from distinct seeds give the same per-attempt probabilities as fresh coins.
heuristics.limitations: s0 is measured on one advice; for the other advice only round-2 rates and 3 collisions are measured. Those show more variation than an independent-pair model predicts, all upward: pooled round-2 ratio 1.033 (2.2 Poisson standard deviations above 1, inside the pre-registered 99% interval), advice 4 2.8 above; 3 collisions in 16 fresh spaces (probability about 0.01 at the v6 rate), two of them in one space (about 0.007); s counts spaces with at least one collision. The v6 run had a disclosed decision rule (submit if s0 >= 0.002), the outcome-selection premise reviewers flagged for v7; the factor 2.2 between s0 and the needed 0.0060 is the margin (3.3 in v8; v10 trades it for a smaller K). The organizer seeds are public and the harness draws no inference.

heuristics.statement: B' candidates with fresh coins are independent; each yields an accepted advice within its cost cap CCAP = 2^26 units (enforced by B''s counter) with probability at least q_c0 = 0.0742.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability: each candidate costs at most CCAP plus one update, so floor(2^32 / (2^26 + 2^13)) = 63 candidates fit B''s budget and, with H3, Pr[B' exhausts its budget before a good advice] <= (1 - 0.0742 x (1 - 0.2831))^63 = 0.0320, including restarts; the claimed 0.40 needs q >= 0.0258 at s = s0. The time cap does not depend on H2.
heuristics.extrapolation: Pre-registration A (proof 4.2): nine B' runs (k = 0: LABEL_B; k = 1..8: new labels) under the shipped program, started together, none stopped or repeated: 65 candidates, 9 accepted (q_c-hat = 0.138; one-sided 95% CP lower bound 0.0742); every candidate ended at most 2^25.848 units, below CCAP, so these are runs of the capped program; whole runs 2^23.4-2^28.2 units. r5-bp-0..4 re-derive every output from its label at the logged counts and audit one other logged attempt each; r5-bpfull executes run k = 1 whole (counted cost equal to the log) and shows both caps acting (candidate 0 stopped at a 2^21-unit candidate cap, B' stopped at a 2^22-unit budget).
heuristics.limitations: Nine runs; q_c0 is a 95% bound. v8's premise on the per-candidate cost is replaced by the cap CCAP; the cap is 2^0.15 above the largest logged candidate, so a candidate that would have been accepted later than 2^26 units is lost, which q_c0 already accounts for (all 9 logged acceptances came within the cap).

heuristics.statement: An advice output by B' has connector acceptance probability q >= 0.10 per attempt with fresh coins, except with probability at most f_up = 0.2831 over B''s coins.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability: a good advice gives 96 accepted attempts within A_ADV = 2^11 except with probability < 2^-41 (Chernoff, mean >= 204.8); weak advice is discarded and B' resumes, so H3 enters as f_up^4 = 0.0065 (at most 4 advice rounds within A_MAX = 2^13) and through H2's bound.
heuristics.extrapolation: Pre-registration A: 128 attempts with each of the 9 advices: 120, 105, 68, 93, 104, 83, 58, 68, 45 accepted (744 of 1,152, all verified); every 99% Clopper-Pearson lower bound is >= 0.255, so all 9 are good and f_up is the one-sided 95% upper bound of 0/9. Organizer-seeded attempts in r5-bp-0..4: 196 of 288 accepted and verified with the public seed (consistent with q >= 0.10 for each advice).
heuristics.limitations: Nine advices; f_up is a 95% bound. Acceptance varies between advices (0.35-0.94), which is why the restart rule exists.
